title: streamlit.pills invokes callback with the value returned by format_func
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If I have `streamlit.pills(label, options, on_change=callback, format_func=formatter)`, `callback` is sometimes invoked not with one of the values of `options`, but with the value returned by `formatter`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

print("RUN!")

if "L" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["L"] = "EN"
if "F" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["F"] = "A"


def set_lang() -> None:
    print(f"Set language to {st.session_state['_L']}")
    st.session_state["L"] = st.session_state["_L"]


def set_fruit() -> None:
    new_fruit = st.session_state["_F"]
    if new_fruit in ["A", "O"]:
        st.session_state["F"] = st.session_state["_F"]
    else:
        print(f"UNEXPECTED: Set fruit to {new_fruit}")


fruits_en = {"A": "apples", "O": "oranges"}
fruits_es = {"A": "manzanas", "O": "naranjas"}

fruits = fruits_en if st.session_state["L"] == "EN" else fruits_es

st.pills("🌐", ["EN", "ES"], required=True, default=st.session_state["L"], key="_L", on_change=set_lang)
st.write(f"Default value: {st.session_state['F']}")
st.pills(
    "😋", ["A", "O"], required=True, default=st.session_state["F"], key="_F", on_change=set_fruit, format_func=lambda f: fruits[f]
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the application as usual
    Console: 
    ```
    RUN!
    ```
1. Click on "ES" 
    Console: 
    ```
    Set language to ES
    RUN!
    ```
    (By the way: Now, no fruit pill is selected, which is also unexpected.)
1. Click on "EN"
    Console: 
    ```
    Set language to EN
    UNEXPECTED: Set fruit to apples
    RUN!
    ```


### Expected Behavior

The callback should always be invoked with one of the options given to `streamlit.pills`, without formatting.

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.14.5rc1
- Operating System: Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2
- Browser: Opera, Firefox, Edge


### Additional Information

_No response_

### Analysis

When `st.pills` (and `st.segmented_control`, which shares the same backend) is used with `format_func`, the widget value is stored and transported as the **formatted string** rather than the raw option. On each script run, `_SingleSelectButtonGroupSerde.deserialize` (in `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/button_group.py`) looks the incoming formatted string up in `formatted_option_to_option_index` to convert it back to the original option. If the lookup fails — which happens here because the `format_func` output changes between runs (English ↔ Spanish via the `fruits` dict) — the serde falls through to `return string_value`, i.e. it returns the formatted string verbatim. This unresolved value is what ends up in `st.session_state["_F"]` and is what the `on_change` callback receives, which is why `set_fruit` is invoked with `"apples"` instead of `"A"`. The follow-up reset by `validate_and_sync_value_with_options` fixes serialization back to the frontend, but it runs *after* the callback has already fired with the formatted string. Closely related to the long-standing serde fragility documented in #8008 and #11541.

### Related Issues

- [#8008 - Selectbox returns old element not in options if format_func returns the same value for old and new options](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8008) — Same root cause family: the selection serde uses `format_func` output as the round-trip key, which breaks when the function isn't stable or one-to-one across reruns.
- [#11541 - ButtonGroup.select() fails when options use format_func or are not primitive strings](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11541) (closed) — Directly about the ButtonGroup (pills/segmented_control) serde mishandling `format_func`; useful prior context and a likely starting point for the fix.
- [#12392 - state management issues with `st.pills` when options change dynamically](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12392) — Another manifestation of the pills/segmented_control state-resync logic misbehaving when the option set/labels change between runs.
